text:
elena: Quick sync — i'm sketching a short, ship-ready set of guardrails + launch checkpoints for multi-region tenant fencing. customer asks: per-tenant geo lock + SLA. want to converge on acceptance criteria today.

sam: SGTM. are we treating this as a runtime routing change or a control-plane policy first?

elena: control-plane policy first. runtime adapters later. goal: be able to declare a "fenced" tenant and have automated routing constraints + soft-failover.

raj: a few quick constraints from infra: cross-region egress cost needs accounting, and we should avoid synchronous cross-region calls on the hot path.

matt: +1. also add requirement for observable invariants: per-tenant routed-region metric, failed-fallbacks, and per-request region tag.

sara: legal/customer asks: some customers require physical-region pinning + audit trail for every decision. that affects our logs + retention policy.

elena: noted. drafting acceptance criteria — propose: 
- "Pinned region honored" for 99.9% of requests under normal capacity
- Transparent fallback: if pinned region unavailable, fallback only to listed secondary regions and emit audit event
- No silent cross-region egress: every cross-region route must be explicit and billed
- Canary policy: 5% traffic + automated rollback after 5m with >1% error delta

sam: that can be our minimal launch bar. we should also include config schema versioning so older private deploys can opt-in.

raj: migration concern: existing tenants without fencing must default to global routing. need a bulk-migration tool + dry-run mode to simulate routing impacts.
matt: test harness idea: replay recorded traffic into a staging slice with fencing toggles to check latency/cold-cache effects.

elena: good. add to checklist: dry-run tool, traffic replay harness, and a cost-estimation report per tenant.

sara: i'll collect customer contract language we need for pinned-region SLAs. also confirm retention window they'll accept for audit logs.

ops-bot: deploy-checklist reminder — please attach a runbook and rollback plan before canary.

sam: launch checklist (quick draft):
1) policy spec checked into repo (schema + validation)
2) control-plane enforcement + audit pipeline plumbing
3) canary slice + replay harness verified
4) cost estimator run and flagged high-cost tenants
5) customer communication templates ready
6) e2e regression prompts and prompt-set-based quality checks

elena: + acceptance tests:
- pinned-region honor test (synthetic traffic)
- fallback policy test (simulate region down)
- billing attribution test (cross-region flagged)
- privacy test (no logs leak tenant IDs across regions)

raj: operational gating: must have auto-eviction throttle to avoid noisy tenants causing cross-region fallback storms.
matt: how do we measure "soft-eviction" impact? need an SLO for failed fallbacks and a back-pressure path.
elena: propose soft-evict = limit that reduces routed QPS by x% before hard-evict. threshold presets: 90th pct latency spike, 3x baseline error rate, sustained 2m.
sara: can we make threshold configurable per-customer in the contract? some want aggressive isolation.
sam: yeah, per-tenant policy overrides but default guardrails shipped. enterprise tenants get a UI + API to set thresholds.

elena: next steps: sam to own schema PR, raj to prototype dry-run tool, matt to wire metrics and tests, sara to own customer SLA language. i'll fold runbook + rollback and coordinate a 30-min demo next Tues.

sam: i'll kick off the schema PR today and tag reviewers.

raj: I'll stand up a minimal replay job using last week's production trace. putting a prototype link in #eng-platform when ready.

matt: i'll add metric panels and a synthetic test in the e2e pipeline.

elena: thanks team. small ask: keep messages here short; i'll compile a single checklist doc after demo and ping product for prioritization. :thumbsup:

sara: FYI — customer "Oceanside Health" asked for a Q2 gated rollout with regional pinning. will bring details to the demo.

ops-bot: note added to roadmap: multi-region fencing (owner: elena, due: 2026-05-15).
